label: station
note: IP-neutral. A space station you fly to, land in and walk round, built from this file alone (src/systems/world/station_hull.gd draws every box from these numbers, src/systems/world/space_station.gd is the node). It is a component: it is not part of any planet. Where it hangs is a 'kind': 'station' landmark naming this file ('station': 'orbital_station'), today over the top of the ringed giant (content/core/planets/ringed_giant.json), where its deck town was; it started over the moon's far side (grit_station.json, 'side': 'far'). Take that landmark out and the station is gone; put it in another planet's landmarks and it is there instead. The plan it follows is docs/station/nitrogen_belt_plan.svg (issue #311): two towers of tall round floors, the top floor the biggest, open space between floors, an elevator up the middle in a glass tube, tunnels between the towers and a covered landing bay. The markets, homes and engine deck are furnished by 'fill' (#315, src/systems/world/station_fill.gd); the top floor and the outpost are still empty shells (#314). Its own frame: y up (level, with its own gravity, like the cruiser), x and z across, the main tower's middle at x = z = 0, y = 0 the market floor (and the bay's deck). Metres.
floors_note: Each tower is a stack of round floors (y: the top of its floor plate, radius: its outer glass wall). The space between one floor's ceiling and the next floor's plate is open to space, crossed only by the glass tube round the elevator. 'rooms': rooms round the outside behind an inner wall with doors, cut by corridors where tunnels leave; false: open from the walkway to the glass (markets). The gap in the middle of each floor (gap_radius) has a glass floor, so you look down the tube through every floor below; the elevator shaft (shaft_radius) runs up its middle, and two bridges join it to the walkway, north-south on one floor, east-west on the next.
fill_note: Issue #315: what is in the floors (src/systems/world/station_fill.gd, the render rules in docs/station/STATION_FILL.md). Each floor id with a 'use' is dressed: favela (the lower homes: rings of shacks, booths and the town's huts packed back to back at r metres, doors facing in or out, depth and h ranges in metres, booth_share/hut_share/stack_share of the pieces, alleys radial alleys alley_half wide and lane_half to the tunnel doors kept clear, lines_per_ring cables and washing lines over each alley), suites (the upper homes: every room a big suite dressed like the cantina's club and the barge), homes (the floor's open_rooms are furnished studios, the rest locked: lounge_at and kitchen_at are fractions of the way from the door to the window, partition_from_window and bed_from_window metres), market (rings of stalls at r metres from the tower's middle, every_m apart round the ring, facing in or out, huts in every other spot of a ring with huts: true (hut_h: the heights they take, a few so they share materials), or a packed ring of shacks and booths like the favela's with pack: true; nothing within lane_half metres of a tunnel door's line; paved in stone flags with tiles round the walkway, stock piled every stock_every_m metres in the gap behind back-to-back rings, lamps lamp posts round the walkway's edge, banners hung from the ceiling), engines (its rooms by turn). Every room's floor, walls and furniture are textured with the station shader's room finishes (carpet, tile, tread plate, marble, velvet, veneer...: StationFill._t), laid out in the room's own frame. A floor's fill is built budget_ms a physics tick (merging merge_verts vertices at a time, a material cut into meshes of at most mesh_verts), and drawn only while the camera is within show_dy metres of its height and show_m of its glass. A floor's 'rooms' may be a count: the suites' floor has 10, of which the two either side of its tunnel's corridor have no door, so 8 suites; the favela's floor has none (it is open from the walkway to the glass).
crowd_note: Issue #315: the people aboard (src/systems/world/station_crowd.gd). floors: how many live on each floor (their home: where they start and come back after respawn_s). They walk the walkway at speed m/s, and by turn (stop_share, elevator_share, tunnel_share, else a stroll) go down an alley to stand stop_s seconds at a stall, booth or shack door (the fill's walking net) or into an open room (room_deep metres in), ride an elevator to another floor that has people (by how many live there, and home_pull of the time home), or cross a tunnel to the other tower's floor. Puppets, like the barge's crowd: built one a frame once the camera is within build_within metres, drawn within people_m and show_dy of the camera, posed from one sampled walk cycle at most anim_budget a frame (every frame within anim_near_m, every fourth out to anim_far_m), shadows within shadow_m. Hurt one and the nearest of the armed_share on your floor within rouse_m (no more than rouse_max at once) become the fighter profile where they stand, rouse_per_tick a tick, back to walking calm_back_s after the alarm is down. looks: content/look/characters.json.
remnant_note: Issue #314: the Remnant's deck (src/systems/world/station_remnant.gd; its look is the fill's use 'remnant'). One whole floor ('tower', 'floor') whose rooms are by turn 'rooms': control (the cruiser's control room with the planet map over its holo table), bunks, armoury, command, mess; its walkway in their colours with a barricade and a checkpoint at its tunnel. Their troopers ('trooper', the commander 'commander') take their posts once the camera is within wake_within metres and sleep past sleep_m. Kill every one and the locals hold the deck for good (Territory place 'station_<landmark id>', saved with the world): the red is painted over in the locals' colours and, locals_after_s seconds later, guard_share of the posts get the locals' guards ('guard').

hatch.note: A hatch in the middle of every tunnel's roof, closed by a shield the air cannot pass and you can: jump up through it (the jetpack) and walk the roof between its railings, out in space, like a bridge; drop back through it to get in.

tunnels_note: Enclosed glass-walled tunnels between two towers ('to': a tower id) at a level both have, or from a tower to the bay ('to': 'bay') at the bay's deck.

elevator.note: A platform rides each tower's shaft, stopping at every floor for wait seconds, at speed m/s between. Stand on it and it carries you on to the next floor the way it is going (turning at the ends); walk onto a floor's bridges while it is elsewhere and it comes to you. The shaft's doors open only on the floor where it has stopped.

bay.note: The covered landing bay: round and 104 m across (bigger than the port pit, for its six pads), its deck level with y = 0, on the far side of 'from' tower's bay tunnel. Its curved wall is open at the back (the tunnel's door) and across mouth_deg of its far side (the mouth, facing away from the tower), closed by a curved energy shield along the wall's line that ships fly through and you cannot walk through. Pads: 'at' is [out toward the mouth, across] in metres from the bay's middle; every ship sits nose out to space. 'ship' parks that ship on the pad (a town 'ship' box, StationHull.town_for: a berth you board like the port's bay ships; 'free': anyone's to fly, story save or not); 'spare' is where a ship bought from T-99 lands (his 'pad'). A parked ship model is 30 to 80 draw calls (the frigate 28, the gunship 60), so only the frigate is parked; the rest are for ships that fly in.

salesman.note: T-99, the station's ship salesman (content/core/npcs/t99.json): his marker on the bay's deck ('at', [out, across] from the bay's middle like a pad), facing 'face'. A ship bought from him lands on the 'spare' pad.

dock.note: Z within radius metres flies you in: round the towers (over_y above or under_y below them, in the station's frame) when you start behind the bay's mouth, out to approach metres off the mouth at hold_y over the deck, in through the shield and to a stop over the dock pad, then turned nose out and set down (ShipPilot's docking autopilot, the same flight as the cruiser's).

outside.note: Where the planet's air is breathable (no harmful_surface, the ringed giant) the station is open to it (SpaceStation.open_air): the bay's shield lets you walk out of the mouth onto the apron, and you can roam outside on the jetpack. Over a gas ball's clouds, drop more than drop_below metres under the lowest floor and you are pulled back into the bay (lines.fell_clouds). Where you cannot breathe it is sealed as before: the shield holds you in and falling out pulls you straight back (lines.fell).
